newsitem.title: UK: Allied Domecq to cut UK spirits prices.
newsitem.headline: Allied Domecq to cut UK spirits prices.

text.p: Drinks and retail group Allied Domecq will cut the price of its leading UK spirits brands by 26p a bottle before the critical Christmas trading period.
The move follows an immediate four percent reduction in tax duty on spirits, equivalent to 26p off a bottle, announced by Chancellor Kenneth Clarke in his budget statement on Tuesday.

"From yesterday we reduced our prices in the pub by a penny a nip. In Victoria Wine we are reducing this week Teacher's Beefeater and Courvoisier. The price of all other brands will be reduced once our current stocks are replenished," said Tony Pratt, director of corporate affairs.
Allied owns Britain's 1,500 Victoria Wine off-licenses.

"The general consumer spending background looks a lot healthier this Christmas, but as always we will have to wait and see how that translates in business in the pubs and offlicenses in the next month," Pratt added.
At a news conference Ian Hannah, president of international brands, said the company plans to spend 4.0 million stg on advertising four brands in Britain on television ahead of Christmas.
The four core UK brands are blended whisky Teacher's, liqueur Tia Maria, cognac Courvoisier and Cockburn port.
In his previous budget Clarke reduced duty on spirits by the same amount for the first time since 1895.
Since last year's cut in duty average prices per bottle of whisky have fallen to 9.85 stg for supermarkets' own label, although the price of brands has risen slightly.
On Tuesday Highland Distilleries, makers of blended Scotch whisky Famous Grouse, said it also hoped to pass on the full saving to customers before Christmas.
